A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MindHier framework. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching, including v2's expanded image galleries.

before.justification: v1 reports original NSD reconstruction results, component ablations, inference timings, per-subject evaluations, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds cross-subject transfer, THINGS-fMRI, quantitative grounding, VQA, and additional efficiency evaluations.

M1.justification: The hierarchical fMRI encoder, MSE/SoftCLIP alignment, two-stage training, and scale-aware autoregressive reconstruction remain unchanged. Added loss-weight and implementation specifications clarify the existing method; the PDFs do not establish a change to its underlying procedure.

E1.justification: v2 expands beyond NSD reconstruction to THINGS-fMRI with three subjects and different acquisition conditions (Appendix I), VQA on reconstructed images (Appendix G), and held-out-subject transfer (Appendix C). Brain grounding and single-subject one-session experiments already existed in v1.

E2.justification: Table 1 removes both Psychometry variants and adds NeuroPictor and MindTuner. Figure 4 adds MindEye2 to the consistency comparison. New comparisons additionally evaluate MindEye and UMBRAE-S1 for grounding and BrainFlora on THINGS-fMRI, substantially broadening the comparison suite.

E3.justification: New protocols include pooled pretraining followed by held-out-subject finetuning for 40 or 1 hour, N=1 versus N=4 candidate selection, and MindEye2 with 10 versus 38 denoising steps. v2 also introduces quantitative grounding metrics, BLIP-2 top-3 VQA evaluation, and joint-subject THINGS training with 7000-dimensional padded inputs. The original NSD protocol and Table S2 experiment remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds sampling-budget and generation-step controls, component-wise and scale-wise latency analyses, and cross-subject data-scarcity testing. VQA cases and expanded reconstruction galleries support new analyses of counting, material, text, and identity failures. The original encoder, layer-mapping, and guidance ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains the same uncertainty values and reporting format. Neither version specifies additional statistical estimation procedures or training-run counts. The four-trial visual comparison is extended to another baseline, while N=1 versus N=4 concerns candidate selection rather than uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Retained MindHier NSD scores and Tables 2–4/S1–S2 are unchanged, but substantial new results appear. VQA accuracy is 43.29% versus MindEye2's 41.71%; THINGS CLIP accuracy is 73.1% versus BrainFlora's 57.6%, although Eff distance is worse at 0.900 versus 0.812. New one-hour cross-subject results show MindHier below MindEye2, including CLIP 80.2% versus 80.7%. Grounding, timing, sampling, and qualitative results are also added.

T1.justification: The alignment equations, token quantization, and autoregressive factorization are retained. Corrections to norm delimiters and feature subscripts are not substantive mathematical revisions. Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The third introduction contribution changes from claiming state-of-the-art semantic and structural fidelity to emphasizing a balance of semantic fidelity, stability, and speed, with prospective real-time brain-computer-interface applications. The central framework, semantic-fidelity claim, and 4.67× speedup claim remain.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive qualifications about poor one-hour cross-subject transfer, attributed to overfitting, and failures involving materials, counting, text, and identity. Appendix F adds an efficiency explanation based on eliminating refinement and inexpensive coarse stages. Its finding that high-resolution stages dominate latency conflicts with the retained main-text explanation that most computation occurs at low resolutions.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies full CLIP patch-token alignment, MSE weight 2×10^5, temperature 0.005, codebook size 4096, ten autoregressive scales, RTX 4090 inference hardware, and THINGS input padding. These refine existing documentation; the principal optimizer settings, training budgets, pseudocode, and code-release promise remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including THINGS-data, BrainFlora, diffusion foundations, and image/video generation works, while removing UniBrain and BrainGuard. The two related-work narratives and the central positioning against static diffusion guidance remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The main section order and most prose are retained, with local copyediting, clearer two-stage-training explanations, revised contribution wording, and updated affiliations and conference headers. The appendix gains sections F–J, acknowledgments are added, and LLM writing assistance is disclosed; this primarily accompanies new content rather than extensive rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables S3–S9 and Figures S4–S9, including four substantial subject-specific galleries. Figure 2 receives clearer feature and mask labels, Figure 4 gains a baseline row, and Table 4's Eff direction arrow is corrected. Existing appendix displays are retained and repositioned.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the evidence beyond v1's NSD-only evaluation through THINGS testing, held-out-subject transfer, sampling and generation-step controls, and downstream grounding/VQA assessments. Explicit failure analyses and missing implementation settings make applicability and reproducibility more assessable. Reporting flaws temper these gains: Appendix F contradicts the retained efficiency explanation and claims stages 0–4 take under 0.1 seconds although Table S7 totals 0.211 seconds. These localized inconsistencies do not outweigh the substantial improvement in validation and transparency.
